transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you for seeing me. I guess what finally made me come in is that at work, I’ll sit down to do something like an EPIC quality report, or I’ll be in a clinic metrics meeting really trying to follow along, and then a few minutes later I realize my mind has gone somewhere else. I’ll be rereading the same numbers over and over, or I’ll notice I missed the main point of what was being discussed.

I know that probably happens to everyone sometimes, so I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s been enough that I thought I should ask about it.
Have you been feeling sad or down when your mind wanders like that?

Not really sad, no. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes, maybe a little embarrassed if I missed something, but I wouldn’t say I feel down when it happens. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge lately?
I don’t think so, not especially. I mean, I can get a little tense if I realize I’ve missed something or I’m behind, but I wouldn’t say I’m walking around anxious or on edge. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling hopeless about the future lately?
No, I wouldn’t say hopeless. I mean, I have moments where I feel irritated with myself, but I still feel like things are basically okay and workable. Hopefully that answers what you’re asking.
Do you have trouble remembering things that happened recently?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think I’ve noticed a big problem with remembering recent things. Maybe little normal things here and there, but nothing that stands out to me as, like, “I can’t remember what just happened.” Is that what you mean?
Do you have trouble focusing on tasks or activities outside of work?

Yes… though honestly it shows up at work too. I mean, I try to be prepared and pay attention, but what finally made me come in was things like starting an EPIC quality report, or sitting in a clinic metrics meeting, fully intending to follow along, and then a few minutes later realizing my mind has wandered so far that I’m rereading the same numbers or I’ve missed the whole point of what was just discussed. It feels embarrassing to say, because I’m not trying to be careless.
Are you having trouble completing tasks or achieving your goals because of your mind wandering?

Yes, I think so… maybe not in a dramatic way, but it does happen. Like after a committee meeting, if someone gives me three or four follow-up items, I’ll do the first one, maybe start drafting the second, and then somehow the email or spreadsheet or final submission just sits there unfinished until someone reminds me. I hate admitting that, because I really do intend to follow through. Does that make sense?
Do you have any recurring thoughts or urges that you feel compelled to repeat over and over?

I don’t think so… not in the sense of feeling like I have to repeat something over and over. I mean, I can overthink things sometimes, like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I have urges or thoughts that feel compulsive. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you find yourself worrying about a wide range of things in your daily life?

I’m not sure I’d say a wide range of things, no. I mean, I worry about normal life stuff, like anyone would, but I don’t feel like I’m constantly worrying about everything all day. At least, I don’t think that’s the main issue for me… is that what you mean?
Do you find that you are often preoccupied with worries about everyday things, even when there is no apparent reason to worry?

Not really, no. I mean, I can worry if there’s an actual problem or deadline, but I don’t feel like I’m sitting around preoccupied with worries when nothing is going on. At least, that’s not how it feels to me. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Do you feel like your mind wandering and trouble focusing are related to feeling overwhelmed or stressed?

I think stress can make it worse, sure, but… I don’t think it’s only when I’m overwhelmed. What finally made me come in is that I’ll sit down to work on an EPIC quality report, or I’ll be in a clinic metrics meeting really intending to follow along, and then a few minutes later I realize my mind has completely wandered. I’ll be rereading the same numbers, or I’ll realize I missed the main point of what someone was saying.

It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I’m trying. It’s not that I don’t care. Does that make sense?
How long have you been experiencing this mind wandering and trouble focusing?

I’d say it really became noticeable after my promotion… so about two years and four months ago. I had more responsibility, a bigger portfolio, and the systems I’d always used to keep myself on track just didn’t seem to hold up as well anymore.

I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I fell apart or anything, but that’s when the mind wandering and focus issues started feeling harder to manage. Does that answer it?
Do you find that your mind wandering and trouble focusing happen in your personal life as well, not just at work?

It’s mostly been obvious at work, I think. That’s where it really shows up because of the EPIC quality reports and the clinic metrics meetings. I’ll sit down fully meaning to follow along, and then a few minutes later I’m rereading the same numbers or realizing I missed the main point of the discussion.

In my personal life… I guess it may happen some, but it’s harder for me to separate out or notice. The work examples are what finally made me feel like, okay, maybe I should ask someone about this. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships or daily activities outside of work due to your mind wandering and trouble focusing?

A little, yes… I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but it has started to affect things outside of just me quietly struggling.

At work, some of my delays have affected clinic reporting deadlines, and I know that makes other teams wait on me, which I feel really bad about. And outside of work, I’ve had to step back from leading parts of the volunteer health workshops because I just couldn’t reliably keep all the planning pieces moving the way I needed to.

So… yes, I guess it is causing some real problems. Does that make sense?
Do you often worry about making mistakes or not doing something perfectly, even when things are going well?

I’m not sure I’d say “often,” exactly. I mean, I do like things done correctly, especially when other people are depending on the work, but I don’t know that I’m constantly worried about perfection when things are going well.

Maybe I can be a little hard on myself sometimes, but… I’m not sure if that’s what you mean. I wouldn’t want to make it sound bigger than it is.
Do you typically feel restless or fidgety when you're trying to focus on a task?

Not really, I don’t think. I mean, I might shift in my chair or pick up a pen like anyone would, but I haven’t noticed feeling especially restless or like I can’t sit still when I’m trying to focus.

For me it’s more… I just lose the thread mentally. But physically fidgety? I don’t think that’s a big issue. Is that the distinction you’re asking about?
Have you experienced excessive worry about a specific situation or thing, such as your health, finances, or relationships, that you find difficult to control?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I worry about normal things sometimes, like anyone would, but I wouldn’t say there’s one specific thing—health or money or relationships—that I’m excessively worried about or can’t control.

At least, nothing that stands out to me that way. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you experienced persistent and excessive worry about everyday things for more than six months?

I don’t think so. I mean, I have day-to-day worries like anyone does, but I wouldn’t describe it as persistent or excessive, especially not for six months or more.

If anything, it comes and goes depending on what’s happening. I don’t feel like I’m worrying about everyday things all the time. Is that the kind of distinction you mean?
Do you think your mind wandering and trouble focusing are related to anxiety or are they a separate issue for you?

I think it feels separate from anxiety, mostly. I mean, I’m not sitting there worrying about something when it happens.

It’s more like… I’ll start an EPIC quality report, or I’ll be in a clinic metrics meeting really intending to follow along, and then a few minutes later my mind has just drifted. Then I’m rereading the same numbers, or I realize I missed the point of what someone was saying.

That’s actually kind of what pushed me to come in, because it’s embarrassing and I don’t want it to affect my work. Does that make sense?
Do you think your mind wandering and trouble focusing would improve if you didn't have to worry about meeting deadlines or making mistakes at work?

Maybe a little, but I don’t think it would go away completely. I’m not always distracted because I’m scared of a deadline or worried I’ll make a mistake.

What finally pushed me to come in is that I can start an EPIC quality report, or sit in a clinic metrics meeting, really intending to follow it, and then within a few minutes my mind has drifted. Then I’m rereading the same numbers or realizing I missed the whole point of the discussion.

So yes, pressure probably makes it feel worse, but the focusing problem seems to happen even when I’m trying and I’m not especially anxious. Does that make sense?
